items.objective: Observe supervised regional anaesthesia practice and explain the drugs and adjuncts used, their intended roles and relevant precautions.
Describe attachments, nerve supply and actions of pectoralis major and pectoralis minor; describe the clavipectoral fascia.
On a specimen or model, describe and demonstrate serratus anterior attachments and actions, and explain relevant clinical anatomy.
Describe the anatomical basis of cubital venipuncture, including relevant superficial venous location and neighbouring structures in a labelled diagram.

items.topicLabel: General Features, Joints, radiographs & surface marking
items.objective: Describe the sternoclavicular, acromioclavicular, carpometacarpal and metacarpophalangeal joints.
Describe and demonstrate the joint type, articular surfaces and movements of the manubriosternal, costovertebral, costotransverse and xiphisternal joints.
Describe and demonstrate the thyroid gland’s location, parts, borders, surfaces, relations, blood supply and applied anatomy. Briefly describe the parathyroid glands.
Describe and demonstrate the extent, formation, relations and branches of the cervical sympathetic chain.
Describe the morphology, relations, blood supply and applied anatomy of the palatine tonsil and the composition of the soft palate.
Describe the position, fibre direction, relations, nerve supply and actions of semispinalis capitis and splenius capitis.

items.topicLabel: Head & neck Joints, Histology, Development, Radiography & Surface marking
items.objective: Demonstrate testing of the muscles of facial expression, extraocular muscles and muscles of mastication, and palpation of the carotid, facial and superficial temporal arteries. Locate the internal and external jugular veins and identify the hyoid bone, thyroid cartilage and cricoid cartilage with their vertebral levels.
Describe the parts, components, blood supply and lymphatic drainage of the penis.
Describe and identify the formation, course, relations and tributaries of the portal vein, inferior vena cava and renal veins.
Describe the sites of portosystemic anastomoses, their applied anatomy and anatomical correlations.
Describe the cranial nerve nuclei of the pons by functional group.
Describe the development of the neural tube, spinal cord, medulla oblongata, pons, midbrain, cerebral hemisphere and cerebellum.
Describe the ultrastructure of nervous tissue.

items.topicLabel: Principles of Genetics, Chromosomal Aberrations & Clinical Genetics
items.objective: Describe the genetic basis of variation, including polymorphism and mutation.
Describe the formation of the extraembryonic mesoderm and coelom, bilaminar disc and prechordal plate.
Describe the indications, process and disadvantages of amniocentesis.
Describe the indications, process and disadvantages of chorionic villus biopsy.

Observe and explain what is measured by the pH meter, paper chromatography of amino acids, protein electrophoresis, TLC, PAGE, ISE electrolyte analysis, ABG analyser, ELISA, immunodiffusion, autoanalyser and DNA isolation from blood or tissue.

items.topicLabel: Introduction to forensic medicine basics of legal procedure.
items.objective: Describe court procedure for a medical witness, covering issue of summons, conduct money, types of witnesses, recording of evidence on oath or affirmation, examination-in-chief, cross-examination, re-examination, court questions and conduct in the witness box, and apply them in a role-play.

In a simulated or supervised setting, examine an alleged accused in a sexual offence case, prepare the report, frame the opinion, preserve and dispatch trace evidence, and discuss how personal views can compromise objectivity and neutrality.

Elicit, document and present a history to establish the diagnosis, cause and severity of heart failure, including presenting complaints, precipitating and aggravating factors, risks, exercise tolerance, sleep changes and features suggestive of infective endocarditis.
Assess the severity of valvular heart disease using clinical, laboratory and imaging findings and describe the level of intervention required, including surgery.
Discuss pharmacology, indications and contraindications for diuretics, ACE inhibitors, beta blockers, aldosterone antagonists and cardiac glycosides in heart failure.

For an adult with a common form of congenital heart disease, elicit, document and present the history, demonstrate the general examination and relevant findings, and formulate, document and present a management plan.

Elicit, document and present a history covering onset, evolution, presenting symptoms, risk factors, family history, comorbidities, complications, medication use and prior atherosclerosis, ischaemic heart disease or coronary syndromes.
Perform, demonstrate and document a physical examination including vascular and cardiac examination appropriate to the presentation.
Generate, document and present a differential diagnosis, prioritizing diagnoses that must be excluded, likelihood and severity.
Discuss the pathogenesis, recognition and management of acute coronary syndrome complications, including arrhythmias, shock, left ventricular dysfunction, papillary muscle rupture and pericarditis.
Elicit, document and present a pneumonia history including illness evolution, risk factors, immune status and occupational risks.
Generate, document and present a differential diagnosis and prioritize it based on the clinical presentation.

Order and interpret investigations appropriate to the presentation, including CBC, PA chest radiography, Mantoux testing, sputum Gram stain and culture with susceptibility, pleural fluid examination and culture, HIV testing and arterial blood gases.

In a simulated case, select and prescribe an appropriate empirical antimicrobial, describing the choice in terms of its pharmacology and antimicrobial spectrum, and revise the prescription when culture and sensitivity results are supplied.

Elicit, document and present a fever history including evolution, pattern, associated symptoms, immune status, comorbidities, risk factors, occupational, travel and environmental exposures, and medication use.
Discuss the pathophysiology, clinical features and management of heat cramps, heat exhaustion and heat stroke.
Discuss the pathophysiology, causes and clinical manifestations of fever of unknown origin in immunocompetent patients, neutropenic patients, hospitalized patients and people with HIV.
Perform a systematic examination to establish diagnosis and severity, including general, skin, mucosal, lymph node, chest and abdominal examination with assessment of the liver and spleen.

Order and interpret investigations based on the fever differential, including CBC with differential, peripheral smear, urinalysis with sediment, chest radiography and other imaging, blood and urine cultures, sputum Gram stain and culture, sputum AFB testing and culture, CSF analysis, pleural and other body fluid analysis, routine stool examination and culture, serology, FNAC, biopsy, bone marrow examination and QBC.
For prolonged fever, explain indications and expected findings for inflammatory and rheumatologic tests, pathogen serology including HIV, and bone marrow aspiration and biopsy.

In a supplied HIV/opportunistic-infection scenario, choose and interpret the indicated CBC, sputum examination and culture, blood culture, stool analysis, CSF analysis and chest radiograph findings in an OSCE or viva setting.
Explain the principles of combination antiretroviral treatment and compare antiretroviral classes, their main effects, adverse reactions and interactions in a supplied HIV/AIDS scenario.
Discuss the pathogenesis of immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) and describe its management.
Explain the principles of HIV post-exposure prophylaxis and describe the regimens used, applying them to a hypothetical exposure scenario.
Describe the workup for the presumed cause and explain the indications for and interpretation of CBC, anti-CCP, RA, ANA, DNA and other autoimmunity tests.
Enumerate indications for plain radiographs of joints and interpret the findings.
Select, prescribe and communicate appropriate medicines for joint pain relief and preventive therapy in crystalline arthropathies.
Select, prescribe and communicate treatment options for systemic rheumatologic conditions.
Elicit, document and present a history that helps distinguish the possible causes of the presenting joint condition.
Perform a systematic examination of all joints, muscles and skin to establish diagnosis and severity.
Define and classify hypertension.

Elicit, document and present a history covering blood pressure duration and levels, symptoms, comorbidities, lifestyle, risks, family history, psychosocial and environmental factors, diet, and previous and concurrent therapy.
Define, describe and classify anaemia by red blood cell size and reticulocyte count.
Elicit, document and present a history covering symptoms, risks including gastrointestinal bleeding, prior history, medicines, menstrual history and family history.
Describe national programmes for anaemia prevention.

items.topicLabel: Acute Kidney Injury and Chronic renal failure
items.objective: State the indications for arterial blood gas analysis and interpret supplied ABG results, identifying the primary disturbance and the degree of compensation.

items.topicLabel: Acute Kidney Injury and Chronic renal failure
items.objective: Describe the evolution, natural history and treatment of acute renal failure.

items.objective: Elicit, document and present a history that differentiates causes of renal disease, distinguishes acute from chronic disease and identifies predispositions, nephrotoxic medicines and systemic causes.

items.topicLabel: Acute Kidney Injury and Chronic renal failure
items.objective: Describe acute renal failure management priorities including diet, volume management, drug-dose adjustment, monitoring and indications for dialysis.

items.topicLabel: Acute Kidney Injury and Chronic renal failure
items.objective: Discuss supportive care in chronic kidney disease, including diet and management of blood pressure, glycaemia, dyslipidaemia, anaemia, hyperkalaemia, hyperphosphataemia and secondary hyperparathyroidism.

items.topicLabel: Acute Kidney Injury and Chronic renal failure
items.objective: Explain how chronic kidney disease affects quality of life, wellbeing, work and family, and incorporate patient preferences into care.
Perform and interpret urinary ketone testing with a dipstick.

Elicit, document and present a history that differentiates causes of diabetes, covering risk and precipitating factors, lifestyle, nutrition, family and medication histories, comorbidities and target-organ disease.

Discuss the pharmacology, indications, adverse reactions and interactions of medicines used to prevent or treat target-organ damage and complications of type 2 diabetes, including neuropathy, nephropathy, retinopathy, hypertension, dyslipidaemia and cardiovascular disease.
Describe precipitants, pathophysiology, recognition, clinical features, diagnosis, stabilization and management of the hyperosmolar nonketotic state.
Elicit, document and present a history to establish the diagnosis, cause and severity of thyroid dysfunction.
Demonstrate correct blood glucose self-monitoring technique and counsel the patient on its use.
In a simulated case, write a thyroxine prescription based on age, sex, clinical findings and biochemical status, then communicate it appropriately to the patient.

Perform and demonstrate a history-guided examination for thyroid dysfunction and its severity, including systemic signs of thyrotoxicosis and hypothyroidism, pulse rhythm, thyroid and lymph node palpation, and cardiovascular findings.
Elicit, document and present a cancer history covering risk factors, symptom duration and evolution to help establish the aetiology.
Describe indications for and interpret chest radiography, mammography, skin and tissue biopsies, and tumour markers used in common cancers.
Using a supplied case, explain how the patient's needs and preferences shape the choice between curative and palliative therapy.
Define and measure obesity in the Indian population context.
Define and measure obesity in the Indian population context.
Elicit, document and present a history covering obesity course, diet, modifiable risks, family history, clues to secondary causes and motivation for weight loss.

Perform, document and demonstrate a history-guided physical examination including general examination, measurement of abdominal obesity, and assessment for signs of secondary causes and comorbidities.
Describe the indications, use and adverse effects of opioid analgesics for cancer pain.
Enumerate indications for endoscopy, colonoscopy and relevant imaging investigations in a scenario of suspected upper gastrointestinal bleeding.
Explain the indications, relevant pharmacology and adverse effects of vasopressors used in the treatment of upper gastrointestinal bleeding.
Identify Vibrio cholerae in a hanging-drop specimen under supervision.
Define and classify headache and describe the presenting features and precipitating, aggravating and relieving factors of its various types.
Elicit, document and present a headache history including aura, precipitating, aggravating and relieving factors, and associated symptoms that help identify the cause.
Generate, document and present a differential diagnosis for headache based on the clinical features.
Describe the pharmacology, doses, adverse reactions and regimens of medicines used for bacterial, tuberculous and viral meningitis.
Elicit, document and present a cerebrovascular history including onset, progression, precipitating, aggravating and relieving factors, and associated symptoms that help identify the cause.
Examine a stroke patient with a speech disorder, document and present the findings, and describe how to distinguish speech disorders by lesion site.
Enumerate indications for surgery in haemorrhagic stroke.
Enumerate and describe the indications and modalities of multidisciplinary stroke rehabilitation.
Elicit, document and present a movement-disorder history including onset, progression, precipitating, aggravating and relieving factors, and associated symptoms that help identify the cause.
Generate, document and present a differential diagnosis for a movement disorder using history and physical examination findings.
Define and differentiate seizures, convulsions and epilepsy.
Classify epilepsy by aetiology and discuss its pathophysiology, clinical evaluation, recognition of different types, diagnosis and diagnostic tests.
Enumerate local venomous snakes and describe the distinguishing marks of each.
Elicit, document and present a snakebite history covering circumstances, timing, snake type if known and symptom evolution.
Perform, document and present a systematic physical examination after snakebite, including general, local, cardiac and neurological examination.
Enumerate indications for antivenom and describe its pharmacology, dosing and adverse reactions, including hypersensitivity.
Describe the diagnosis, initial approach, stabilization and treatment of bee stings and other envenomation.
Identify and describe the toxidrome suggested by the observed findings.
Discuss the toxicology, clinical features, complications, prognosis and management approach for organophosphate and carbamate poisoning.
Observe and describe the role and functions of a poison centre in suspected poisoning, document the observation in the logbook and discuss it in a viva.

Discuss the aetiopathogenesis, clinical presentation, identification, functional changes, acute care, stabilization, management and rehabilitation of acute confusional states.
Discuss the aetiopathogenesis, clinical presentation, identification, functional changes, acute care, stabilization, management and rehabilitation of vascular events in older adults.
Discuss the aetiopathogenesis, clinical presentation, identification, functional changes, acute care, stabilization, management and rehabilitation of depression in older adults.
Describe the aetiopathogenesis and clinical presentation of dementia in older adults and discuss acute care, stabilization, management and rehabilitation.

Discuss functional changes, acute care, stabilization, management and rehabilitation in older adults undergoing surgery.
Discuss the aetiopathogenesis, clinical presentation, identification, functional changes, acute care, stabilization, management and rehabilitation of degenerative joint disease.
Discuss the aetiopathogenesis, clinical presentation, identification, functional changes, acute care, stabilization, management and rehabilitation of falls in older adults.
Discuss the aetiopathogenesis, presentation, identification, functional changes, acute care, stabilization, management and rehabilitation of common fractures in older adults.

Discuss the aetiopathogenesis, clinical presentation, identification, functional changes, acute care, stabilization, management and rehabilitation of visual abnormalities and visual loss in older adults.
Discuss the aetiopathogenesis, clinical presentation, identification, functional changes, acute care, stabilization, management and rehabilitation of personality changes in older adults.
Discuss the aetiopathogenesis, clinical presentation, identification, functional changes, acute care, stabilization, management and rehabilitation of osteoporosis in older adults.
Discuss the aetiopathogenesis, clinical presentation, identification, functional changes, acute care, stabilization, management and rehabilitation of stroke in older adults.

Elicit, document and present a medical history that helps establish the aetiology of an infectious disease, covering the evolution and pattern of symptoms, risk factors, and occupational and travel exposure.
Perform a systematic examination to establish the diagnosis and severity, including general, skin, mucosal, lymph node, chest and abdominal examinations, with examination of the liver and spleen.
Discuss the aetiopathogenesis, clinical presentation, identification, functional changes, acute care, stabilization, management and rehabilitation of hearing loss in older adults.
Discuss the aetiopathogenesis, presentation, complications, assessment and management of nutritional disorders in older adults.
Discuss the common causes, clinical features and management of urinary tract infections, pyelonephritis and prostatitis.

Discuss common causes, clinical features and management of infections of the skin, muscles and soft tissues.
Discuss the common causes, aetiopathogenesis, clinical features and management of bacterial zoonoses, including leptospirosis, brucellosis, plague and anthrax.
Discuss the pathogenesis, clinical features and management of rickettsial diseases, especially scrub, epidemic and endemic typhus.
Discuss the aetiopathogenesis, clinical features, complications and management of herpes simplex virus infections.
Discuss the aetiopathogenesis, clinical features, complications and management of varicella-zoster virus infections.
Discuss the aetiopathogenesis, clinical features, management and prevention of rabies.
Discuss the aetiopathogenesis, clinical features and management of candidiasis.
Discuss the aetiopathogenesis, clinical features and management of aspergillosis.
Discuss the aetiopathogenesis, clinical features, complications and management of amoebiasis.

Describe the microbiology of the tubercle bacillus, transmission, pathogenesis, clinical evolution and natural history of pulmonary and extrapulmonary tuberculosis, including lymph node, bone and CNS forms.
Describe the epidemiology of antituberculous drug resistance and the predisposing, microbial and treatment-related factors that determine it.
Elicit, document and present a tuberculosis history covering risks, contacts, cough, fever, anorexia, weight loss, haemoptysis and extrapulmonary symptoms.
Discuss the origin, indications, administration technique, efficacy and complications of BCG vaccination.
Discuss the pharmacology, indications, contraindications, interactions and adverse reactions of antituberculous agents.

Demonstrate and perform a systematic examination appropriate to suspected tuberculosis, including general, chest, lymphatic and relevant CNS examination. Assess volume loss, mediastinal shift, percussion, breath sounds and added sounds.

Order and interpret diagnostic tests for a patient whose history and examination suggest tuberculosis, including CBC, PA chest radiograph, Mantoux test, sputum smear, culture and sensitivity, pleural fluid examination and culture, and HIV testing.
Elicit, document and present a medical history that differentiates the aetiologies, severity and precipitants of obstructive airway disease.

Discuss and describe the therapies for obstructive airway disease, including bronchodilators, leukotriene inhibitors, mast cell stabilizers, theophylline, inhaled and systemic steroids, oxygen and immunotherapy.

Describe the epidemiology, aetiopathogenesis, clinical features and complications of viral hepatitis.
Enumerate the causes of hyperandrogenism and describe its investigation and management, distinguishing common presentations from those that need urgent workup.
Compare femoral neck and intertrochanteric fracture cases by mechanism, presentation, investigation and management principles, including communication of functional consequences.

items.objective: Demonstrate and document the clinical examination of a thyroid swelling, then discuss its differential diagnosis and management.

Connect arterial occlusion mechanisms to examination findings and justify investigation and treatment priorities in simulated cases.
Distinguish forms of gangrene and use simulated cases to explain amputation principles and assessment priorities.
Distinguish DVT and varicose vein presentations and defend investigation and management approaches in simulated cases.
Compare lymphoedema, lymphangitis and lymphoma presentations and defend an investigation and management approach for each.
